extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Chamber members, business leaders, employers, and policymakers interested in employment/labor policy and advocacy
extracted.subtask_description: A topical hub for producing and publishing employment-law and labor-policy advocacy materials (letters, regulatory filings, reports, testimony, press releases, and analysis) aimed at agencies, Congress, and the public. The page organizes content types, policy priorities, and engagement channels used by the U.S. Chamber in employment law advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content types / publication formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter by Content Type — Article; Explainer; Guide; In the News; Letter To Congress; Letter To President; Letter to Federal Agency; Policy Position; Press Release; Opinion; Regulatory Filing; Report; Testimony To Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site categorizes its output into these discrete formats; creators and consumers should use these labels when producing or searching for materials (e.g., submit a 'Letter to Federal Agency' when addressing rulemaking). No additional formatting/submission rules are provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy goals / policy priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chamber works to 'protect opportunities for independent contractors, promote needed immigration reforms to welcome global talent to the American workforce, and preserve every American’s right to work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content and filings should align with these stated priorities — materials advancing independent contracting, specific immigration reforms, or right-to-work positions reflect the Chamber's focus and are therefore the expected substantive stance for advocacy outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement channels / target institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Chamber works with leaders at the U.S. Department of Labor, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the National Labor Relations Board, Congressional committees, and state legislatures to advance employment policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing advocacy or regulatory materials, target these agencies and bodies as primary audiences and channels for influence (e.g., send letters, filings, testimony to these entities). The page implies these are the proper recipients for policy interventions, though no procedural instructions are given here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Featured topics / substantive focus areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics listed on the page include Anti-Human Trafficking; Unions; Worker Safety; Workforce; and related labor/employment subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials should be organized and framed around these featured topics when relevant. The presence of these topic headings signals priority issue-areas for content and advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs and events as outreach formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chamber runs events and programs (examples shown: Military Spouse Employment Summit; AI + Work; Midwest Institute) as part of its workforce and employment policy engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond written submissions, the organization uses events and hybrid meetings to advance policy goals and disseminate analysis; contributors may participate via panels, testimony, or presentations tied to these events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational authorship / expert roles
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists senior staff and vice presidents (e.g., Senior Vice President, Employment Policy Division; Vice President, Immigration Policy; Vice President, Labor Policy) as responsible parties for content and policy positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authoritative materials and official positions are expected to be issued or endorsed by these organizational leaders; drafts intended as official Chamber positions should be coordinated with the relevant policy lead indicated.
